missing_theorem: For a special family (e.g. p = 2^k·a + 1 with a fixed), a folding identity for the continued fraction of p/A (A built from 2^k) produces, for every k, an A with HJ-length λ(p/A) ≤ 3 and (A/p) = −1 — an ES₅ certificate for every member.
yield: partial (one more thin family; no transfer to general primes)
status_ref: Thin families proved by forced-budget windows: (J)62–(J)80 (3·2^s + 1, 7·4^s + 9, 63·2^s + 1, …), FRONTIER §1, §7.8 (15·2^s + 1, 4^s + 297 open). Folding constructions are not in the repo. Transfer blocked: (J)76 (menu ladder collapses to B1/B2), (J)84 (side numbers irreducible at a general prime).
barrier: B1 (a thin family is a congruence/polynomial family; works only via forced factorisation), (J)84 Thm A
new_ingredient: folding lemma for CF of a/q^k as a source of forced bounded-length expansions
next: Test whether the folding lemma applied to p/2^j (j ≈ k/2) for p = 15·2^s + 1 yields length-≤3 expansions with a non-residue denominator for s ≤ 60; if yes, it is a candidate attack on the open family 15·2^s + 1.
note: Only value: a possible new tool for the open thin families of §7.8; Niederreiter bounds partial quotients, not CF length, so the fit is uncertain.

role: pointwise existence from polylog expected count via independence + concentration (Erdős–Tetali template)
missing_theorem: At each prime p the ES certificate events are 'Erdős–Tetali independent': there is a decomposition into events with Janson Δ ≤ μ²/(C log p) and μ ≥ C log p, so P(no certificate) ≤ p^{−2} in an honest probability space attached to p.
yield: ES (if such a space existed at fixed p)
status_ref: BRAINSTORM/s9_janson_dependency.md (108 283 primes ≤ 3·10⁶): word-level Δ/μ = 3.6 → 9.4, μ²/2Δ = 0.85 → 1.82 ≪ log p; level-granularity expected count (0.44 → 0.97)·log p is critical. s9_lower_tail_literature.md: Erdős–Tetali choose the random set; ES's set is fixed (no probability space at one p, B6).
note: Pass 1: covered.

role: calibration only (logical direction: coverage ⇒ unbounded multiplicity, converse of what ES needs)
missing_theorem: none. The Erdős–Turán direction for ES is already known: R(p) ≥ exp(c log p/log log p) infinitely often (Linnik). Erdős–Fuchs does not apply (the ES generating series Σ q^{tuv−u−v} is not f(z)²).
status_ref: BM_CORRECTED_COUNT Prop 3.1 (Linnik large values); METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K (generating series); Pass 1.

role: function-field large-q limit (Sawin–Shusterman template) proving an ES-strength statement over F_q[T], then transfer
missing_theorem: For fixed degree n and q ≥ q₀(n), every (monic, irreducible) P of degree n in F_q[T] has an ES/U word certificate.
status_ref: EXSET_FUNCTION_FIELD.md §0 items 5–6 (PROVED): the large-q exceptional density is a Chebotarev statistic ρ_{n,p} of a monodromy group, and the boundary n-cycle shows a POSITIVE proportion c′_n qⁿ of irreducible P have no nontrivial word — the large-q limit makes the lottery exactly random at fixed mass, so it proves failures, not ES. Item 12: no integer transfer.
barrier: B3/fixed mass (large q does not raise the expected count), B-fin (no transfer)
note: Instructive: the large-q method is the cleanest proof that a fixed-mass lottery fails a positive proportion of the time.

role: transfer of proved F_q[T] ES variants to ℤ (identify their last ingredient)
missing_theorem: A ℤ-analogue of the decisive F_q[T] step: either (a) a characteristic degeneracy making the size-obstructed class trivially solvable (char 2, 3: 1 ≡ −1 resp. −2), or (b) a modulus confining all primes to few classes (T^q − T). Neither has a ℤ-analogue.
status_ref: FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md §§5–6 ('Why this exists over F₂ and not over ℤ'), FUNCTIONFIELD_ES2/3; Pass 1: the last ingredient is a characteristic/degree degeneracy, not an RH-type input; the fixed-q density theorem is the analogue of Vaughan (B6).
barrier: B-fin (no transfer), B6 for the density theorem
note: Gap to ES: the ℤ problem has neither degeneracy.

role: calibration: count deficit ⇒ failure is provable (Pomerance–Weingartner) — the opposite direction of ES
missing_theorem: none for ES. Lesson: any ES argument must use m = 4 specifically or a threshold p₀(m) (numerator blindness); PW's mechanism (Brun–Titchmarsh upper bound on solvable primes when expected count ≈ (log p)³/m ≪ 1) has no content at fixed m = 4.
status_ref: Pomerance–Weingartner arXiv:2511.16817 (as catalogued); EXCEPTIONAL_MN.md; FRONTIER §3 numerator blindness, §4 screen 2.

role: derandomised certificate search with a provable step bound (AKS template: an identity certifies quickly)
missing_theorem: An explicit deterministic procedure finds an ES certificate for every prime p in (log p)^{O(1)} steps (equivalently, a certificate always exists among polylog-size explicitly indexed candidates).
status_ref: False i.o. for candidate sets bounded by small parameters: H4_NOT_POLYLOG.md (forest witnesses not polylog), POINTWISE_OMEGA13 Thm 5.1 (W(p) ≥ exp(c(log p)^{1/4}…) i.o.); B1 Thm M/C for congruence-defined procedures. AKS works because the property (primality) is an algebraic identity; ES existence is not.
note: Pass 1: covered (z52b_dividing #238, #309). Same architecture as Z3100.

role: pointwise existence at every prime via a primality-forced descent on the fundamental unit / CF cycle of ℚ(√p) (Legendre's negative-Pell proof as template)
missing_theorem: For every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4), p > p₀: some element of the principal reduction cycle of ℚ(√p) (a convergent P_k/Q_k of √p, or an ambiguous form in the cycle) yields an ES₅ certificate, i.e. a bichromatic edge of the forest F_p — proved, like N(ε_p) = −1, by a descent that uses that p has no non-trivial factorisation.
status_ref: Legendre: x² − py² = −1 is solvable for every prime p ≡ 1 (4) (pointwise, no counting) — one of very few every-prime existence theorems, driven by unique factorisation of p. Repo: FRONTIER §7.2 lists 'Pell / class-group cycle data' as an open root source (Astra's open questions); (J)84 Prop 4.2 closes CF-norm windows m = |P_k² − pQ_k²| with gcd(Q_k, m) = 1 (always (p/m) = +1, never Jacobi-forced), so the cycle must be used as other coordinates, not as windows. Cheap check (this pass, scripts/z52d_avenue_P06_pell_roots.py, timeout 60): taking as roots the principal-cycle data of √p (all norms |P_k² − pQ_k²| incl. 1, and all partial quotients) and looking only at their forest neighbours (uv | p+u+v), 6 of 1610 primes p ≡ 1 (4) < 3·10⁴ have no bichromatic edge: 577, 1129, 7057, 8761, 11257, 19441. So the one-step version is false at small p (rate ≈ 0.4 %, not obviously decaying); only full components or other cycle coordinates remain.
barrier: B2 (the cycle has ≍ √p·L(1,χ_p)/log ε_p … elements but the certificate class is still tied); (J)84 Prop 4.2; B1 under Dickson for fixed-length cycle data
new_ingredient: Legendre-type primality descent (unique factorisation of p·y²) — uses primality of the target, which is what fails for composite d in negative Pell
next: Extend the check to whole forest components of the cycle roots and to p ≤ 10⁷; if failures persist at a non-decaying rate, the Pell-cycle root source is in the same position as fixed/least-QNR roots ((J)106) and should be closed.
note: Inverted minimal pair: for ES composites are easy, so primality would have to be used as Legendre uses it (as a descent closure), not as a difficulty.

role: calibration: ES is immune to covering-type (periodic-witness) failure
missing_theorem: No residue class r (mod M), gcd(r, M) = 1, consists of ES-failing primes from some point on — indeed ES holds for almost all primes in every such class.
status_ref: Shift-uniform exceptional set in progressions ((D)30, FRONTIER §5.1: E(I) ≪ H exp(−c(log H)^{3/4}) on intervals and progressions with small q) + Dirichlet: a full class of failures is impossible. Pass 1: the (★)-zeros 409, 577, 5569, … spread over several classes mod 840.
next: None; the general lemma is a corollary of (D)30 and could be stated in one line.
note: Plausibility 3 = essentially in hand; yield none for ES.

role: calibration only (dataset of small-count mixed-sum problems)
missing_theorem: none.
status_ref: Pass 1: arXiv:0901.3075 (Sun) states mixed-sum conjectures with ≍ log n counts; no ES quantity; exception lists not enumerated.

role: calibration: PW's failure mechanism needs m → ∞ (numerator blindness check)
missing_theorem: none for ES: PW's lower-bound-on-failures argument uses expected count (log p)³/m ≪ 1 at p ≈ m², so it is vacuous at fixed m = 4.
status_ref: EXCEPTIONAL_MN.md; FRONTIER §3 numerator blindness (threshold-robust form relative to PW Thm 1.2).
note: Same content as Z0566.

role: calibration: a restricted variant (no denominator divisible by 3) with a single sporadic prime failure (241)
missing_theorem: Restricted statement: every prime p ∉ {3, 241} has a solution of 4/p with 3 ∤ xyz. It is stronger than ES (a sub-lottery), so it can only be a component if it were somehow easier — no mechanism suggests that.
status_ref: Pass 1: for n ≤ 400 the no-3 failures are exactly the multiples of 3 and 241 (scripts/z52b_p1_U09_parity_no3.py). 241 ≡ 1 (240), least QNR 7, (2/241) = (3/241) = (5/241) = +1. Not in repo.
next: Explain 241: list its 8 solutions and show each has 3 | xyz via the mod-3 structure of the (★)/Type I words with small C; check whether the same happens for the next prime with least QNR ≥ 7 and p ≡ 1 (mod 120).
note: Curiosity; a single sporadic failure of a sub-lottery is what the zero law predicts for a smaller mean.

role: calibration: the isosceles (degenerate) locus is obstructed exactly at p ≡ 1 (4) by a mod-4 divisor condition
missing_theorem: none: (4x − 2p)(4z − p) = 2p² (and the y = z analogue) forces A ≡ 2 (4), B ≡ −p (4) with B ∈ {1, p, p²}, impossible iff p ≡ 1 (4); so every solution at a hard prime is scalene.
status_ref: PROVED (elementary) in BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md:17; Pass 1 checked the algebra.
barrier: none (miniature mod-4 obstruction, unrelated to the polylog lottery)

role: calibration: no parametrisation has a power-size reservoir (expected count polylog in p for ranges up to p^A)
missing_theorem: none: Σ_{C ≤ X} τ(4Cp+1)/φ(4C) ≈ log p·log X, and two-parameter forms give log p·log²X — polylog for X = p^A.
status_ref: FRONTIER §1 (polylog expected count), §3 B3 (scale constraint); Pass 1: minimal C > √p for only 0.1 % of primes.

role: covering-system re-indexing: each certificate (C, a) certifies the class p ≡ −(4C)^{−1} (mod a)
missing_theorem: Every prime p > p₀ lies in a class p ≡ −(4C)^{−1} (mod a) for some C and some a ≡ −1 (mod 4C), a² ≤ 4Cp + 1 — the divisor form of (★) re-indexed by the divisor.
status_ref: FRONTIER §2.1 divisor form; the moduli a grow with p, so this is the B2 event, and any fixed finite set of (C, a) is a congruence covering (B1).
note: Pass 1: covered.

role: two-sided concentration: pointwise polylog upper bound for f(p) (as a calibration of the lower-bound problem)
missing_theorem: f(p) ≪ (log p)^A for every prime p.
yield: none (an upper bound proves nothing about existence)
status_ref: R(p) injects into Type II solutions (PARITY_AUDIT Lemma 2.1′) and R(p) ≥ exp((log 2/L_Lin − o(1)) log p/log log p) for infinitely many p ≡ 1 (4) (BM_CORRECTED_COUNT Prop 3.1, Linnik), so f(p) is not polylog-bounded. Best pointwise upper bound: f(p) ≪ p^{o(1)}-type divisor bounds; |E(p)| ≪ p^{2/5+o(1)} (FRONTIER §3 tied modulus).
barrier: Linnik large values (FRONTIER §4 screen 7: one-sided only)
note: Pass 1's data (max f/log² = 1.90 at p ≤ 1.2·10⁴) is the bulk; the large values occur at p ≡ 1 mod highly composite numbers.

role: exceptional-set bound via a sieve for simultaneous multiplicative-set membership of the linear forms 4Cp + 1, uniform in the number K of forms
missing_theorem: Uniform K-fold sieve: #{p ≤ X : for all C ≤ K, 4Cp + 1 has no divisor ≡ −1 (mod 4C)} ≤ e^{O(K)}·X·∏_{C ≤ K}(1 − δ_C(X)) with K = X^{1/s}, i.e. a fundamental lemma in dimension growing with the sieve level — this would give a power-saving (or better) exceptional set.
yield: partial (exceptional set beyond exponent 3/4; no individual p)
status_ref: This is the RLD-U / FL∞ statement of FRONTIER §7.12 (EXSET_ARITH_JANSON_OPUS Cor 6.1, CONDITIONAL; EVIDENCE to 10¹⁰), attacked by six lanes and a board in z51 without movement (BREADTH_Z45 §16). For fixed K, Hooley-type methods apply; the membership 'subset products avoid −1 mod 4C' is not a Landau set for C > 1 (it depends on the joint multiset of prime factors).
barrier: B6; CRT supply cap 3/4 for CRT architectures ((D)24); growing-dimension sieve
next: Read Hooley (1976) ch. 5 only to extract the dependence on K of the error terms for K simultaneous two-squares-type conditions at C = 1 multiples (4Cp+1 with only primes ≡ 1 mod 4); compare with the FL∞ requirement.
note: Recurring target with §7.12; judged as hard as the pointwise problem there (Assessment).

role: effective asymptotic + numerical verification (Vinogradov → Helfgott): make an all-large-p statement explicit below 10¹⁸
missing_theorem: Any effective statement 'R(p) ≥ 1 (or f(p) ≥ 1) for all p > p₀' with p₀ ≤ 10¹⁸; given R ∈ ℤ, H⁻_BM(ε, 10¹⁸) with ANY ε > 0 suffices.
status_ref: Pass 1: only main terms are effective (M_BM ≥ (3/(16π²) − o(1)) log²p via Burgess; explicit Burgess constants available); no asymptotic lower bound for R, f_I, f_II or ES₅ exists, even conditionally (FRONTIER §2.4). The gap is qualitative, not a constant.
barrier: B2, B6 (no single-p asymptotic to make effective)
note: Same as PILOT Z2068.

role: contradiction from a counterexample via algebraic rigidity in a field attached to p (Mihăilescu/Stickelberger template)
missing_theorem: If ES(p) fails (or R(p) = 0), then some nontrivial relation holds in Cl(ℚ(√p)), the unit group, or a Stickelberger-annihilated module of ℚ(ζ_q) for auxiliary q, and that relation is impossible.
status_ref: No candidate relation is known. Related closures: B2 Thm 2.2 (class-number identities, Heegner/Hecke encodings are two-coordinate slices); TWO_POWER_LADDER Thm 3.2 (Stickelberger component sees only S, ES datum is the norm D; m = 2 coincidence is BM/T1); (J)82 (class-group composition adds reachability, never existence). At odd squares all Type I/II certificates fail, so the relation must be false at n = m² — i.e. it must use (·/p).
barrier: T1 (the contradiction must fail at squares), B2, class-not-parity
next: Write the R(p) = 0 condition at a single level C as a statement in the ray class group of conductor 4C (all prime factors of 4Cp+1 generate a subgroup avoiding −1) and check whether a Stickelberger annihilator constrains it for C ≤ 10 at the (★)-failure primes 409, 577.
note: Rigidity theorems work on equations with few solutions; ES failure is a conjunction of ≍ p non-events, which is the obstacle.

role: calibration only (search algorithms for thin Diophantine problems)
missing_theorem: none: ES(p) is a finite O(p²) search per p, verified to 10¹⁷–10¹⁸; lattice-reduction search methods add nothing to a proof.
status_ref: FRONTIER §1 (verification), §3 B-fin (finite search); Pass 1 (Booker–Sutherland arXiv:1903.04284).

role: pointwise logarithmic lower bound via an auxiliary L-function with forced vanishing (Goldfeld–Gross–Zagier template)
missing_theorem: There is an L-function (or family) L_p whose value or vanishing order controls R(p) − M_BM(p), and an auxiliary object with forced high-order vanishing whose repulsion gives R(p) ≫ (log p)^δ.
status_ref: The only L-value in R(p) is in the main term: BM_LVALUE Thm A (T(p) ∝ L(1,χ_p)²; M_BM ≥ 0.9225·M₀ at p ≡ 1 (8) via Stephens) — so the GGZ-type lower bound is already unnecessary for the main term. R − M_BM is a sum over ≍ p levels of order-≥3 character noise (Eisenstein-only, METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K), with no L-function encoding it; producing one is H⁻_BM.
note: Pass 1: no L-function for R(p).

role: contradiction from a counterexample via a Frey-type object (FLT template)
missing_theorem: To a prime p with ES(p) false attach an object (Galois representation, modular form, curve) whose properties are impossible. Any such construction from 'all Type I/II certificates fail' must break at odd squares n = m², where all Type I/II certificates do fail (T1) — so the impossibility must use the quadratic character of p.
status_ref: Pass 1: for C = 1, R = 0 at that level ⟺ Σ_{d | 4p+1} χ_{−4}(d) = τ(4p+1) (divisor form only). (J)97: a disproof would need a 'prime T1'; the dual Frey object would be a proof that none exists. FRONTIER §7.15.
barrier: T1 (object must not exist at squares), non-locality (failure = ≍ p non-events), B2
